findings.title: Unscoped DOM query lets padding test pass silently
findings.problem: The new 'does not collapse the body top padding to zero' test selects via document.body.querySelector('[class*="pt-"]'), which matches the first element anywhere in the document body with a pt- class, not necessarily the popup's own body container.
findings.impact: The assertion `expect(bodyEl?.className).not.toMatch(/!pt-0\b/)` also passes when bodyEl is undefined (optional chaining yields undefined, which does not match the regex), so the test gives false confidence and can pass or fail based on an unrelated DOM node rather than verifying the actual CodeBlockExpandPopup body padding regression it is meant to guard.
findings.recommendation: Scope the query to the rendered dialog (e.g. via getByRole('dialog') or the Popup's own content container) and assert a specific positive expectation such as toHaveClass('!pt-2') instead of a negative match that silently passes on a missing element.
